intro: Here in Edirne province stands the complex Sinan called his masterwork: the Selimiye Mosque, raised in 1569–1575. Look up at its dome. Resting on eight piers, it is wider than that of Hagia Sophia.
history: Sinan was past eighty when he built Selimiye, and here he solved the problem of his working life. He pushed the piers carrying the dome out to the edges of the space, and won a single undivided volume inside. The dome, 31.25 metres across and resting on eight piers, is wider than that of Hagia Sophia. And the mosque was never meant to stand alone: the complex was designed together with its colleges, its market row and its timekeeper's house.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the main dome and the eight elephant-foot piers. Look for the muezzin's platform and the tile panels, and end your walk in the Arasta market.
facts: Did you know? One marble column beneath the muezzin's platform carries an upside-down tulip. The story goes that the ground belonged to a tulip grower who resisted the endowment, and that the motif records his stubbornness. At 31.25 metres, the dome is wider than that of Hagia Sophia — the goal Sinan worked towards his whole life, and reached after eighty. By pushing the piers into the walls, he won a single volume broken by no column, so the mihrab is visible from every point in the mosque.
outro: This brings our visit to the Selimiye Mosque to an end. Before you go, a small request: please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. Let this masterwork keep waiting, unharmed, for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
